parakeet: I want to begin by laying everything on the table. I don't come here to prove that God or Jesus isn't real. That's my personal conclusion. But I'm not interested in forcing it on anyone. I'm simply offering my perspective, inviting you to listen, consider, and decide for yourself. Our worldviews and the beliefs we hold most dear ought to be ours, not trophies we collect from others. My goal isn't to win by knocking down your faith. Rather, I want to share what I've learned, then step back and let you weigh it for yourself. Any change of heart or mind must be yours, freely arrived at by critical thinking and reasoning. Have you ever felt pressured to believe something just because someone else told you it was true? That's not what I'm trying to recreate here. True conviction isn't contagious. You can't catch it like a cold. Real belief is something each of us cultivates through our own reasoning and experience. I can tell you why I believe or don't believe, but I can't, nor do I wish to make you believe the same way. Your journey is yours alone. It's like brewing coffee. I can hand you the beans, but you still have to do the brewing yourself. So what counts as a victory? It isn't me hearing someone say, okay, you convinced me. A real victory is you saying, I've studied, I've questioned, I've weighed the evidence, and here's where I stand. If someone only changes because they feel pressured or persuaded, that isn't a win. It's a hollow switch. Victory is internal for you, not a trophy I collect when someone changes their mind. In short, I value honest inquiry over coercion and authentic self-held convictions over superficial conversions. If anything I share today resonates, I encourage you to own that resonance by doing your own study and reflection. That's the only way any belief, yours or mine, can stand on solid ground.
